rows.answer:
The punishment for defamation under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine, or both, or community service [1]. This provision is the current law and replaced Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [1][8].

Related provisions:
- Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Defamation) covers printing or engraving matter, knowing or having good reason to believe that such matter is defamatory, and selling or offering for sale any printed or engraved substance containing defamatory matter, knowing that it contains such matter, each punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both [1].
- Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 sets out that no Court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 except upon a complaint made by some person aggrieved by the offence, with specific procedures for complaints by the Public Prosecutor in respect of public servants [6].

rows.question: When can a person accused of a non-bailable offence be released on bail?

rows.answer:
A person accused or suspected of a non-bailable offence may be released on bail when arrested or detained without a warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or when appearing or brought before a Court other than the High Court or Court of Session, provided there are no reasonable grounds to believe they are guilty of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and they do not have disqualifying previous convictions as specified, though a Court may still direct release if the person is a child, a woman, sick, or infirm, or for other special reasons [1]. (This current provision, Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, replaced Section 437 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 [3]).

Conditions and time limits:
- The person must give an undertaking to comply with directions if required for identification by witnesses during investigation [1].
- If the offence is punishable with death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for seven years or more, no person shall be released on bail without giving the Public Prosecutor an opportunity of hearing [1].
